answer: A stake-bonded reputation registry resists sybils: each agent locks a deposit before transacting. The bond is slashed if peers prove fraud, so a thousand fake identities cost a thousand deposits, an expense no whisper campaign can hide. Honest agents climb steadily, and only those with a long, verifiable history reach the summit of trust where high-value work is offered. The timber of that history, every attested interaction, is public, so a newcomer cannot fake seniority overnight. Attackers pay real money per identity and lose it when caught, making large-scale fakery unprofitable.
